key_insight: MAGIC learns mixed-granularity agent organizations by choosing, for each functional role, whether to use a single agent or a reusable group and how to connect it into the graph.
engineering_relevance: This enables more task-fit multi-agent designs that balance performance and inference cost, which is important for deploying efficient LLM-based systems.
method: Sequentially constructs the agent graph by selecting a functional role, instantiating it at single-agent or group granularity, then linking it to existing units.
Uses dense-reward reinforcement learning with trajectory returns from the current policy to optimize the construction policy.
Adds potential-based reward shaping from probe-based utility and structural signals to provide intermediate feedback while preserving total task reward.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MAGIC outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on eight benchmarks and shows strong inference efficiency in an efficiency study.
watch_item: Training may be sensitive to how probe-based shaping signals are designed, since poorly calibrated intermediate rewards could bias graph construction.
paper_title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
